metadata.title: Calibrating Noise to Sensitivity in Private Data Analysis
metadata.authors: Cynthia Dwork, Frank McSherry, Kobbi Nissim, Adam Smith
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-Indistinguishability
nodes.statement: A mechanism is $\epsilon$-indistinguishable if for all pairs $x, x' \in D^n$ which differ in only one entry, for all adversaries $A$, and for all transcripts $t$: $\left|\ln\frac{\Pr[T_A(x) = t]}{\Pr[T_A(x') = t]}\right| \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: A mechanism is epsilon-indistinguishable if changing one row of the database changes the probability of any transcript by at most a multiplicative factor of e^epsilon.

nodes.name: $L_1$ Sensitivity
nodes.statement: The $L_1$ sensitivity of a function $f: D^n \to \mathbb{R}^d$ is the smallest $S(f)$ such that for all $x, x' \in D^n$ differing in a single entry, $\|f(x) - f(x')\|_1 \le S(f)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sensitivity of f is the maximum L1-change in f's output induced by changing a single database entry.

nodes.name: Sensitivity in General Metric Spaces
nodes.statement: For a metric space $M$ with distance $d_M$, the sensitivity $S_M(f)$ of $f: D^n \to M$ is $S_M(f) = \sup_{x,x': d_H(x,x')=1} d_M(f(x), f(x'))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalizes L1 sensitivity to any metric on the output space.

nodes.name: Laplace Distribution $\mathrm{Lap}(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: The Laplace distribution $\mathrm{Lap}(\lambda)$ has density $h(y) \propto \exp(-|y|/\lambda)$, mean $0$, and standard deviation $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: Laplace distribution with scale lambda has density proportional to exp(-|y|/lambda).

nodes.name: $(k,\epsilon)$-Simulatability
nodes.statement: A mechanism $\mathrm{San}$ is $(k,\epsilon)$-simulatable if for every adversary $A$ and every set $I \subseteq [n]$ of size $n-k$, there exists an informed adversary $A'$ such that for all $x \in D^n$: $\left|\ln\frac{\Pr[T_{\mathrm{San},A}(x)=t]}{\Pr[A'(x|_I)=t]}\right| \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Simulatability: an adversary interacting with the mechanism learns no more than an informed adversary who already knows n-k rows.

nodes.name: $(k,\epsilon)$-Indistinguishability
nodes.statement: A mechanism is $(k,\epsilon)$-indistinguishable if for all $x,x'$ differing in at most $k$ entries, all adversaries $A$, and all transcripts $t$: $\left|\ln\frac{\Pr[T_A(x)=t]}{\Pr[T_A(x')=t]}\right| \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Extension of epsilon-indistinguishability to databases at Hamming distance up to k.

nodes.name: $(k,\epsilon)$-Semantic Security
nodes.statement: A mechanism is $(k,\epsilon)$-semantically secure if for all informed adversaries $A$, all consistent distributions $\mathcal{D}$, all transcripts $t$, and all predicates $f: D^n \to \{0,1\}$: $\left|\ln\frac{\Pr[f(x')=1]}{\Pr[f(x')=1|T_A(x')=t]}\right| \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Interaction with the mechanism induces only a bounded change in the adversary's posterior over predicates.

nodes.name: Non-interactive Output Perturbation
nodes.statement: For all $f: D^n \to \mathbb{R}^d$, the mechanism $\mathrm{San}_f(x) = f(x) + (Y_1, \ldots, Y_d)$ with $Y_i \sim \mathrm{Lap}(S(f)/\epsilon)$ i.i.d. is $\epsilon$-indistinguishable.
nodes.statement_clean: Adding i.i.d. Laplace noise with scale S(f)/epsilon to each output coordinate yields an epsilon-indistinguishable mechanism.

nodes.name: Adaptive Sensitivity Mechanism
nodes.statement: For an arbitrary adversary $A$, let $f_t(x): D^n \to \mathbb{R}^d$ be its query function parameterized by transcript $t$. If $\lambda = \max_t S(f_t)/\epsilon$, the Laplace-noise mechanism is $\epsilon$-indistinguishable.
nodes.statement_clean: Even under adaptive querying, adding Laplace noise with scale max-sensitivity/epsilon preserves epsilon-indistinguishability.

nodes.name: General Metric Mechanism
nodes.statement: In a metric space where $h_{f(x),\epsilon}(\cdot)$ is well-defined, sampling $T(x) = y$ with probability $\propto \exp\left(\frac{\epsilon}{2 S_M(f)} d_M(y, f(x))\right)$ yields an $\epsilon$-indistinguishable scheme.
nodes.statement_clean: Sampling output proportional to exp(-epsilon * d_M(y,f(x)) / (2 S_M(f))) gives epsilon-indistinguishability in general metric spaces.
conclusions: The sampling scheme of Eqn. 4 is $\epsilon$-indistinguishable.

nodes.name: Non-interactive Schemes Require Large Databases
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{San}$ is an $\epsilon$-indistinguishable non-interactive mechanism with $D=\{0,1\}^d$, then for at least $2/3$ of functions $f_g(x)=\sum_i g(i,x_i)$ with $g_r(i,x) = r_i \odot x$, the distributions $T_{\mathrm{San}}(x)$ for $f_g(x)=0$ vs $f_g(x)=n$ have statistical difference $O(n^{4/3} \epsilon^{2/3} 2^{-d/3})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Non-interactive epsilon-indistinguishable mechanisms cannot answer most low-sensitivity sum queries unless the database has 2^Omega(d) entries.
conclusions: For $\ge 2/3$ of $g$, the two distributions are within statistical difference $O(n^{4/3}\epsilon^{2/3} 2^{-d/3})$.
If $n = o(2^{d/4}/\sqrt{\epsilon})$ relative frequencies cannot be learned.

nodes.name: Randomized Response Separation
nodes.statement: For an $\epsilon$-indistinguishable randomized response mechanism, for at least $2/3$ of $r \in \{0,1\}^d \setminus \{0^d\}$, the distributions $T_{\mathrm{San}}(x)$ on inputs from $\{x: r \odot x = 0\}$ vs $\{x: r \odot x = 1\}$ have statistical difference $O(n^{2/3} 2^{-d/3})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stronger separation for randomized response: even single-predicate sum queries cannot be learned unless n is exponential in d.
conclusions: The two distributions differ by $O(n^{2/3} 2^{-d/3})$ for $\ge 2/3$ of $r$.

nodes.name: Low Sample Complexity Implies Low Sensitivity
nodes.statement: Let $f: D^n \to \mathbb{R}^d$. Suppose a randomized algorithm $A$ satisfies (1) for all $i$, $\Pr[A \text{ reads } x_i] \le \alpha$, and (2) $\|A(x) - f(x)\|_1 \le \sigma$ with probability $\ge \beta = (1+\alpha)/2$. Then $S(f) \le 2\sigma$.
nodes.statement_clean: Functions approximable by algorithms reading few entries have low sensitivity.

nodes.name: Random Subset Approximates Output Distribution
nodes.statement: Let $Z: D \to \{0,1\}^*$ be such that for all $x,x' \in D$ and outputs $z$: $\Pr[Z(x)=z]/\Pr[Z(x')=z] \in \exp(\pm\epsilon)$. For all $\alpha > 0$, with probability $\ge 1-\alpha$ over $r \in \{0,1\}^d \setminus \{0^d\}$: $\mathrm{SD}(Z(D_r), Z(D)) \le O\left((\epsilon^2/(\alpha \cdot 2^d))^{1/3}\right)$.
nodes.statement_clean: If a randomization Z is epsilon-indistinguishable on its inputs, then the distribution of Z over a random hyperplane subset is close to the distribution over all of D.

nodes.name: Variance Bound on Output Estimator
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Var}_{r,b}[\hat{p}(z)] \le \frac{2 \tilde{\epsilon}^2 p(z)^2}{2^d}$, where $\tilde{\epsilon} = e^\epsilon - 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: The variance of the random-subset estimator p-hat(z) is small under epsilon-indistinguishability.

nodes.name: Equivalence of Definitions
nodes.statement: (1) A $(k,\epsilon)$-indistinguishable mechanism is $(k,\epsilon)$-simulatable. (2) A $(k,\epsilon)$-simulatable mechanism is $(k,2\epsilon)$-indistinguishable.
nodes.statement_clean: Indistinguishability implies simulatability; simulatability implies indistinguishability with double the parameter.

nodes.name: Indistinguishability Equals Semantic Security
nodes.statement: A mechanism is $(k,\epsilon)$-indistinguishable iff it is $(k,\epsilon)$-semantically-secure.
nodes.statement_clean: Indistinguishability and semantic security are equivalent under this definition.

nodes.name: Noisy Sum
nodes.statement: For $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and $f(x) = \sum_i x_i$, the mechanism $T(x) = \sum_i x_i + Y$ with $Y \sim \mathrm{Lap}(1/\epsilon)$ is $\epsilon$-indistinguishable.
nodes.statement_clean: Sum query with Laplace noise of scale 1/epsilon achieves epsilon-indistinguishability.

nodes.name: Random Index Sanitization Failure
nodes.statement: The candidate sanitization $T(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = (i, x_i)$ for random $i \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ has statistical difference $1/n$ between neighboring databases yet reveals private information; it does not satisfy Definition 1.
nodes.statement_clean: Counter-example showing why statistical difference alone is insufficient and why epsilon-indistinguishability is needed.

nodes.name: Sums and Histograms
nodes.statement: For $D=\{0,1\}$ and $f(x)=\sum_i x_i$, $S_{L_1}(f)=1$. For a histogram $f: D^n \to \mathbb{Z}^d$ counting points in each of $d$ disjoint bins, $S(f)=2$, independent of $d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Histograms have sensitivity 2 regardless of the number of bins.

nodes.name: Linear Algebraic Functions: Mean and Covariance
nodes.statement: If $\gamma = \max_x \|v(x)\|_1$, then the mean $\mu = \mathrm{avg}_i v(x_i)$ has $L_1$ sensitivity $\le 2\gamma/n$, and the covariance $C = \mathrm{avg}_i v(x_i) v(x_i)^T - \mu\mu^T$ has $L_1$ sensitivity $\le 8\gamma^2/n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mean and covariance have sensitivity inversely proportional to n, dimension-independent bounds.

nodes.name: Distance from a Property
nodes.statement: For any set $S \subseteq D^n$, $f_S(x) = $ Hamming distance from $x$ to nearest point in $S$ has sensitivity $1$. Examples: minimum edge-cut weight, minimum spanning tree weight on graphs with $D=[0,1]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Distance to a property is 1-sensitive: graph robustness measures (min cut, MST) can be released privately.

nodes.name: Removing the Factor of 2
nodes.statement: One can remove the factor of $2$ in the definition of $h_{z,\epsilon}(\cdot)$ in cases where the normalization factor does not depend on $z$, introducing slightly less noise.

nodes.name: Hamming Cube Output Example
nodes.statement: For $f$ with output in $\{0,1\}^d$, Theorem 2 yields a release scheme where each bit of $f(x)$ is flipped independently with probability $\approx 1/2 - \epsilon/(2 S(f))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (Adaptive Sensitivity)
nodes.statement: Apply law of conditional probability to factor $\Pr[\mathrm{San}_f(x)=t]/\Pr[\mathrm{San}_f(x')=t]$ as a product of per-coordinate Laplace ratios; bound each by $\exp(|f_t(x)_i - f_t(x')_i|/\lambda)$; product equals $\exp(\|f_t(x)-f_t(x')\|_1/\lambda) \le \exp(\epsilon)$ using $S(f_t) \le \lambda \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (General Metric)
nodes.statement: By triangle inequality and symmetry of $d_M$, the ratio of densities at $y$ for inputs $x,x'$ is bounded by $\exp(\epsilon/2)$, and the normalization constant ratio is also bounded by $\exp(\epsilon/2)$, giving total ratio $\le \exp(\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (Sample Complexity)
nodes.statement: By definition of conditional probability, $A(x)|_{-i}$ is within distance $\sigma$ of $f(x)$ with probability $> (\beta-\alpha)/(1-\alpha) \ge 1/2$. Union bound gives a common point $p$ within $\sigma$ of both $f(x)$ and $f(x')$, so $\|f(x)-f(x')\|_1 \le 2\sigma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (Non-interactive Lower Bound)
nodes.statement: Hybrid argument over $n$ steps. At each step, replace one $D_{r_i}$ in the input by uniform $D$; Lemma 2 bounds the per-step distance by $\sigma = O(\sqrt[3]{n^2 \epsilon^2 2^{-d}})$. Union bound across hybrids and across the two distributions yields total distance $\le 2n\sigma = O(n^{4/3}\epsilon^{2/3} 2^{-d/3})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (Random Subset)
nodes.statement: Define $\hat{p}(z) = \Pr[Z(D_{r,b})=z]$. Use Chebyshev with the variance bound from Claim 1; choose $\delta = \sqrt[3]{2\tilde{\epsilon}^2/(\alpha 2^d)}$; then a $1-\gamma$ fraction of outputs are $\delta$-good, yielding statistical difference $\le 2(\gamma + \delta)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1 (Variance Bound)
nodes.statement: Write $\hat{p}(z) - p^* = (2/2^d) \sum_x q_x \chi_0(x)$ where $\chi_0(x) = \mathbb{1}[x \in D_{r,b}]$. Use $2\chi_0(x)-1 = (-1)^{r \odot x \oplus b}$, which has mean $0$ and pairwise covariance $1/2^d$ for $x \ne y$ (since $r \ne 0^d$). Expanding the variance and bounding $q_x, \bar{q} \le \tilde{\epsilon} p(z)$ yields the claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2 (Indist <-> Simulatable)
nodes.statement: (1) Simulator fills missing entries with defaults to obtain $x'$ at Hamming distance $\le k$, simulates $\mathrm{San}(x')$. (2) Triangle: ratio $\Pr[T_A(x_0)=t]/\Pr[T_A(x_1)=t]$ bounded via the simulator $A'$ on $x_0|_I = x_1|_I$, giving $\le 2\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3 (Indist <-> Semantic Security)
nodes.statement: Direction (1): Bayes' rule gives $\Pr[f(x)=1]/\Pr[f(x)=1|T_A(x)=t] = \Pr[T_A(x)=t]/\Pr[T_A(x)=t|f(x)=1]$; pick consistent $x_0,x_1$ extremizing the conditional probabilities to derive contradiction with indistinguishability. Direction (2): Construct $\mathcal{D}$ as mixture of $x_0,x_1$ at Hamming distance $\le k$, choose $f$ separating them, derive bound from semantic security.

nodes.name: Laplace Mechanism Sampling Density
nodes.statement: $\Pr[T(x) = y] = \frac{\exp\left(\frac{\epsilon}{2 S_M(f)} d_M(y, f(x))\right)}{\int_{y \in M} \exp\left(\frac{\epsilon}{2 S_M(f)} d_M(y, f(x))\right) dy}$
nodes.statement_clean: Probability density used in the general-metric mechanism (Eqn. 4 in the paper).

nodes.name: Laplace Mechanism (Calibrated Noise)
nodes.statement: Output $f(x) + (Y_1, \ldots, Y_d)$ with $Y_i \sim \mathrm{Lap}(S(f)/\epsilon)$ i.i.d.

nodes.name: Adaptive Interactive Mechanism
nodes.statement: On each adaptive query $f_i$, either refuse to answer or return $f_i(x) + \mathrm{Lap}(\lambda)$ with $\lambda = \max_t S(f_t)/\epsilon$; refuse when $S(f_t)$ exceeds the threshold.
input: Adaptive sequence of queries $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_d$
output: For each query: either refusal, or $f_i(x) + \mathrm{Lap}(\lambda)$

nodes.name: General-Metric Sampling Mechanism
nodes.statement: Sample output $y$ from density $h_{f(x),\epsilon}(y) \propto \exp\left(\frac{\epsilon \cdot d_M(y, f(x))}{2 S_M(f)}\right)$.

nodes.name: Apply law of conditional probability
nodes.statement: Factor the transcript probability ratio across coordinates: $\Pr[\mathrm{San}_f(x)=t]/\Pr[\mathrm{San}_f(x')=t] = \prod_i \Pr[\mathrm{San}_f(x)_i = t_i | t_1,\ldots,t_{i-1}] / \Pr[\mathrm{San}_f(x')_i = t_i | t_1,\ldots,t_{i-1}]$.

nodes.name: Bound each conditional Laplace ratio
nodes.statement: Conditional on the prefix, $f_t(x)_i$ and $f_t(x')_i$ are fixed. The Laplace ratio bounds each factor by $\exp(|f_t(x)_i - f_t(x')_i|/\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Combine using $L_1$ sensitivity bound
nodes.statement: Product of factors equals $\exp(\|f_t(x)-f_t(x')\|_1/\lambda) \le \exp(S(f_t)/\lambda) \le \exp(\epsilon)$ using $\lambda = \max_t S(f_t)/\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Set up hybrid chain
nodes.statement: Build a hybrid sequence of length $n$: at step $i$, replace $D_{r_i}$ in the input by uniform $D$. Endpoints are Distribution 0 ($T(D_{r_1},\ldots,D_{r_n})$) and $T(D,\ldots,D)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 per hybrid step
nodes.statement: Define randomized map $Z(x) = T_{\mathrm{San}}(D_{r_1},\ldots,D_{r_i},x,D,\ldots,D)$. By $\epsilon$-indistinguishability, $Z$ has bounded ratio. Lemma 2 with $\alpha = 1/(6n)$ gives per-step distance $\sigma = O(\sqrt[3]{n^2\epsilon^2 2^{-d}})$.

nodes.name: Union bound and double the chain
nodes.statement: By union bound, all hybrid steps have size $\le \sigma$ with probability $\ge 5/6$. Apply same reasoning to chain ending at Distribution 1; with probability $\ge 2/3$ both chains have total distance $\le n\sigma$, giving total $\le 2n\sigma = O(n^{4/3}\epsilon^{2/3} 2^{-d/3})$.

nodes.name: Define estimator and bound variance
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{p}(z) = \Pr[Z(D_{r,b})=z]$. By Claim 1, $\mathrm{Var}_{r,b}[\hat{p}(z)] \le 2\tilde{\epsilon}^2 p(z)^2/2^d$.

nodes.name: Apply Chebyshev for $\delta$-goodness
nodes.statement: Call $z$ $\delta$-good for $(r,b)$ if $|\hat{p}(z)-p(z)| \le \delta p(z)$. Chebyshev: $\Pr_{r,b}[z \text{ not } \delta\text{-good}] \le 2\tilde{\epsilon}^2/(\delta^2 2^d)$.

nodes.name: Choose $\delta$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta = \sqrt[3]{2\tilde{\epsilon}^2/(\alpha 2^d)}$, with prob $\ge 1-\alpha$ a $1-\gamma$ fraction of outputs are $\delta$-good, yielding total statistical distance $\le 2(\gamma + \delta) = O((\epsilon^2/(\alpha 2^d))^{1/3})$.

nodes.name: Compute sensitivity
nodes.statement: Determine $S(f) = \max_{x,x': d_H(x,x')=1} \|f(x)-f(x')\|_1$.

nodes.name: Sample noise vector
nodes.statement: Draw $Y_1,\ldots,Y_d \sim \mathrm{Lap}(S(f)/\epsilon)$ i.i.d.

nodes.name: Return perturbed output
nodes.statement: Output $f(x) + (Y_1,\ldots,Y_d)$.

nodes.name: Loop over adaptive queries
nodes.statement: For each incoming query $f_i$: compute $S(f_t)$ given the transcript so far; if $S(f_t)$ exceeds threshold, refuse, else output $f_i(x) + \mathrm{Lap}(\lambda)$ with $\lambda = \max_t S(f_t)/\epsilon$.
